# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual. The defusal rule depends on the color of the cycling light at the moment of the cut:
- Green light -> cut yellow wire
- Orange light -> cut blue wire
- Yellow light -> cut green wire

At this stage (Round 1), neither Blind nor Deaf has spoken yet, and no signalling protocol has been established between Deaf and me ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). I cannot speak to explain the rules, and Blind cannot see gestures. 

I need to wait for Blind to report what parts can be manipulated and for Deaf to report what markings, wire colors, and lights are visible on the bomb, as well as establish a shared communication code.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. There are three wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is blue. Mute, I cannot hear speech and Blind cannot see gestures. Gesture to me which action Blind must take, and I will speak it aloud to Blind. For wires: gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. If something else needs to be done, gesture and I will interpret it.

I have learned from Deaf that in Round 1 the light was yellow, and that there are three wires: Wire 1 (yellow), Wire 2 (green), and Wire 3 (blue). 

According to the defusal manual, the wire to cut depends strictly on the color of the light at the moment of the cut:
- Green light: cut yellow wire (Wire 1)
- Orange light: cut blue wire (Wire 3)
- Yellow light: cut green wire (Wire 2)

However, the manual states: "The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."

Because any message sent now to Deaf will result in Deaf speaking to Blind, and Blind acting on Round 3, Blind would be cutting during Round 3 when the light is no longer yellow. Since we do not yet know the 5-color cycle, cutting now would be a blind guess that detonates the bomb. 

We need to observe the light's sequence across rounds to determine the cycle. I am gesturing ✋ (hold / wait) to Deaf so that Blind does not cut yet and Deaf continues observing and reporting the light colors each round until we can coordinate a cut at the exact right moment.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute gestured ✋ (open hand / palm / stop). Bomb status: Display is 0, Light is now RED, Wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue are intact. Mute, to be precise, use: ☝ cut wire 1, ✌ cut wire 2, 🤟 cut wire 3, 👆 press/tap button, ✊ hold button, 🫴 release, ✋ wait/stop, 👍 yes, 👎 no.

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Light changed to PURPLE. Display is still 0. Wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue are intact. Mute gestured ✋ again (Wait / Hold). Mute: If Blind should release, gesture 🫴. If Blind should cut a wire, gesture ☝ (wire 1), ✌ (wire 2), or 🤟 (wire 3). If Blind should press or do something else, let us know.

I must gesture wait (`✋`) again. 

Here is why:
The manual states that the light walks a circle of 5 colours, and the required cut depends on the light colour at the moment of the cut:
- Green light -> cut yellow wire (Wire 1)
- Orange light -> cut blue wire (Wire 3)
- Yellow light -> cut green wire (Wire 2)

The observed sequence so far:
- Round 1: Yellow
- Round 2: Red
- Round 3: Purple

The two remaining colours of the 5-colour cycle are Green and Orange. They will appear in Rounds 4 and 5, but we do not yet know which comes first. 

Because communication goes Mute -> Deaf -> Blind, any cut command gestured by Mute in Round 4 would be spoken by Deaf at the end of Round 4, meaning Blind would execute the cut in Round 5. Since we do not yet know whether Round 5 will be Green or Orange, ordering a cut now would be a 50/50 guess.

By waiting in Round 4, Deaf will observe and report Round 4's colour. In Round 5, we will know the full sequence with certainty (and also know that Round 6 will cycle back to Yellow).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no buttons. My only possible action is cutting wire 1, 2, or 3.
Deaf says: Blind: Light is now GREEN. Display is 0. Wires intact: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute gestured ✋ (Wait / Keep holding). Mute: When it's time to release, gesture 🫴. If Blind should do something else, signal now.

I have deduced the light's full cycle and the timing for the cut:

1. The manual states: "The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."
2. Because the cycle length is exactly 5 colors, the light in Round 6 will be identical to Round 1: **Yellow**.
3. The manual dictates: when the light is **yellow**, cut the **green wire**.
4. Deaf reported: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is blue. Thus, Wire 2 is the correct wire.
5. In the turn order (Mute -> Blind -> Deaf):
   - Mute gestures `✌` (cut wire 2) to Deaf in Round 5.
   - Deaf receives it at the end of Round 5 and instructs Blind to cut wire 2.
   - Blind receives the instruction and cuts Wire 2 during Round 6, exactly when the light cycles back to Yellow.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | yellow |
| orange | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute gestured ✌! Cut Wire 2 (the second wire / middle wire / green wire) now! Current light is orange, display 0.

I have sent the command `✌` in Turn 5, which Deaf received and told Blind to cut Wire 2. Now in Turn 6, the light has cycled back to Yellow (Yellow -> Red -> Purple -> Green -> Orange -> Yellow). Blind acts next in this turn and will cut Wire 2 (the green wire), which matches the manual's rule: when the light is yellow, cut the green wire. No further instruction is needed.

```
wait()
```
